newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end soft as profit-taking continues.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end soft as profit-taking continues.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down slightly Tuesday for the second consecutive session as investors ignored the latest data showing strong growth and continued to take profits on last week's gains, brokers said.
The market was expected to be broadly stable Wednesday with some further profit-taking likley, they added.

Tuesday, the General Index .IGRA dipped 0.07 percent to 1,748.55 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL fell 0.38 percent to 2,546.86 points, according to bolsa figures given at the market's 1330 local time/1430 EDT close.
In a total of 1,546 trades, volume was a meager 22.4 million soles ($8.4 million).

"The market is gradually consolidating -- just like the Peruvian economy," Julio Alcalde of local brokerage MGS y Asociados said. "This means investors are looking at the medium- and long-term, because at the moment share prices are at their proper value."
The National Institute of Statistics and Information (INEI) said Monday Peru's year-on-year Gross Domestic Product growth in March was 5.2 percent, compared with a 0.9 contraction in March last year.

Benchmark Telefonica del Peru edged up 0.15 percent to 6.41 soles in 30 percent of the day's total trade. ING Barings analyst Patrick Jurczak raised his rating on Telefonica del Peru SA Tuesday to buy from hold.
Electricity distributor Edelnor dropped 3.17 percent to 2.14 soles in volume of 55,000 shares.
The country's brewery group Union de Cervecerias Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA fell 1.02 percent to 1.94 soles in volume of 433,000 shares.
